gaps: Cost per person hurt avoided is not computed here. A sketch for the LTN program [inference — mine]: the 152 candidate cells hold about 318 injury crashes a year (1,592 in 2021-2025), about 400 people hurt a year at SF's 1.26 people per crash; at -22% to -35% that is about 90 to 140 fewer a year, against $5.6M to $7.8M a year of build cost over 10 years plus about $5.2M upkeep, so roughly $80,000 to $145,000 per person hurt avoided, before bus gates and boundary effects.

SF's candidate cells are larger (median 0.257 km2) than most London LTNs; Furlong's largest size class (100,000 m2 and over) did about half as well (-22%, -37% to -4%), so the London headline -35% overstates what SF-size cells would do.

Each group's share inside built cells is not computed; target_share gives the residential street-class share and the cells' citywide share (11% of injury crashes) separately. A crash-to-cell join by group would fix this.
